notes: Cross-verse split. The relative the ASV supplies over a verbless clause with an articleless adjectival predicate is marked `added` under rule 55 at PRO.30.12 and PRO.30.24, but here it was folded into the adjective under rule 41's articleless-attributive clause. Nothing in the source licenses the difference: גִּבּוֹר is the predicate of the clause, not an attributive inside a nominal expression, as the identically shaped `הַנְּמָלִים עַם לֹא־עָז` of 30.25 and `שְׁפַנִּים עַם לֹא־עָצוּם` of 30.26 show by being rendered as main clauses with the copula on the predicate. The English relative also governs the coordinated finite clause *And turneth not away for any*, which an attributive frame cannot carry. The one unit S:[s002] T:t003 t004 t005 is therefore split into an `added` unit for the relative and an aligned unit giving the adjective its own English with the construction-supplied copula under rule 20. Every other unit is unchanged.
